skill.name: mermaid-diagrams
skill.description: Create Mermaid diagrams for architecture, flows, data models, and software documentation.
skill.summary: Create maintainable Mermaid diagrams for software documentation.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: AI review found the high static score is mostly Markdown false positives from Mermaid code fences, diagram examples, and example URLs. The only confirmed issue is optional export guidance in SKILL.md that suggests installing Mermaid CLI and running a Docker container with the current directory mounted. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: External rendering commands are presented as export options.
remediation.suggestion: State that npm, mmdc, and Docker commands require explicit user approval and trusted local inputs before execution.

remediation.issue: The Docker example mounts the current working directory.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a dedicated diagram directory and a read-only mount in examples that render Mermaid files.

static_findings.snippet: Transform complex technical concepts into clear, maintainable diagrams that can be version-controlle
Mermaid syntax is intuitive and follows a consistent pattern across all diagram types:
- **VS Code** - Preview with Markdown Mermaid extension
- **Export** - PNG, SVG, PDF via Mermaid Live or CLI
7. **Validate syntax** - Test in Mermaid Live before committing
- **Export for presentations** - Use Mermaid Live or CLI for high-res exports
- **[Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live)** - Interactive editor with instant preview and expo
- **VS Code Extension** - "Markdown Preview Mermaid Support" for live preview
8. **Use enum/check constraints** - Enforce valid values at database level
3. **Comment Extensively** - Use `%%` comments to explain complex relationships
5. **Version Control** - Store `.mmd` files alongside code for easy updates
- `layout: elk` - Advanced layout for complex diagrams (requires integration)
- Mermaid CLI - `npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` then `mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png`
- [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live) - Online editor with PNG/SVG export
description: Comprehensive guide for creating software diagrams using Mermaid syntax. Use when users
Create professional software diagrams using Mermaid's text-based syntax. Mermaid renders diagrams fr
All Mermaid diagrams follow this pattern:
- VS Code - With Markdown Mermaid extension
- [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live) - Online editor with PNG/SVG export
- Mermaid CLI - `npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` then `mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png`
- **Breaking characters** - Avoid `{}` in comments, use proper escape sequences for special characte
- **Syntax errors** - Misspellings break diagrams; validate syntax in Mermaid Live

content.user_title: Create Mermaid Diagrams for Software Docs
content.value_statement: Software teams need diagrams that stay close to code and documentation. This skill helps create clear Mermaid diagrams for architecture, flows, schemas, and models.
actual_capabilities: Selects Mermaid diagram types for architecture, flows, databases, classes, and timelines.
Provides syntax guidance for class, sequence, flowchart, ERD, C4, state, git, Gantt, and chart diagrams.
Explains theming, styling, layout, links, tooltips, and embedding options.
Helps structure diagrams for Markdown, GitHub, GitLab, VS Code, and documentation tools.
Offers best practices for readable, version-controlled diagrams.
limitations: Does not render diagrams by itself; users need Mermaid-compatible tools.
Does not validate every Mermaid version or renderer-specific syntax.
Does not inspect live systems or generate diagrams from repositories automatically.
Large architectures may need manual scoping and multiple diagrams.

use_cases.title: Document a Product Workflow
use_cases.description: Create flowcharts that show user journeys, decisions, success paths, and error paths for feature planning.

use_cases.title: Explain System Architecture
use_cases.description: Build C4 and sequence diagrams that show systems, containers, components, users, and service interactions.

use_cases.title: Model Application Data
use_cases.description: Create ERD and class diagrams for schema design, domain modeling, and implementation reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Flowchart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid flowchart for [process]. Include start, key decisions, success path, and failure path.

prompt_templates.title: Model Domain Classes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid class diagram for [domain]. Show main entities, relationships, key attributes, and important methods.

prompt_templates.title: Map Service Interactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid sequence diagram for [workflow]. Include actors, services, messages, alternate paths, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a C4 View
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid C4 diagram for [system]. Show users, external systems, containers, boundaries, and communication protocols.

output_examples.input: Map checkout flow with authentication, address validation, payment, and confirmation.
output_examples.output: A focused flowchart plan with login checks, address validation, payment approval, order creation, and failure paths.

output_examples.input: Explain a notification service that consumes order events and sends email or SMS messages.
output_examples.output: A C4 component view showing the event queue, notification worker, provider clients, database, and external delivery services.

output_examples.input: Design database relationships for users, posts, comments, tags, and likes.
output_examples.output: An ERD outline with primary entities, junction tables, foreign keys, cardinality, and polymorphic relationship notes where needed.

best_practices: Start with one concept and add details only when they improve decision-making.
Match diagram names to code, database, or domain terms used by the team.
Validate diagrams in the target renderer before publishing documentation.
anti_patterns: Combining architecture, data model, and user journey details in one crowded diagram.
Using unclear labels that do not match implementation or business language.
Adding styling before relationships and scope are accurate.

faq.question: What diagram types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers class, sequence, flowchart, ERD, C4, state, git graph, Gantt, pie, and bar diagrams.

faq.question: Can it render Mermaid diagrams directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides Mermaid syntax and guidance. Rendering requires a compatible editor, documentation tool, CLI, or online renderer.

faq.question: Is this useful for architecture reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps create C4, sequence, and flow diagrams that clarify system boundaries and service interactions.

faq.question: Can it help with database design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ERD guidance for entities, keys, relationships, cardinality, and schema documentation.

faq.question: Does it work with GitHub and GitLab?
faq.answer: Yes. Mermaid diagrams can be embedded in Markdown where those platforms support Mermaid rendering.

faq.question: How should large systems be documented?
faq.answer: Split large systems into focused diagrams. Use separate views for context, containers, components, data, and workflows.
